(By Sri.L.P. Suresh.,Adv.,)
 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 26.7.2021.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
Sharath Kumar R vs Ramakrishna on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167837568/
1 On 26.7.2021 at about 2.20 p.m. the petitioner came from Pantharapalya to Nayandahalli junction in his motor cycle bearing No. KA-41-EQ-1389 and when he was proceeding on Mysore road to Nayandahalli junction to Pantharapalya the driver of the Piaggio Ape Xtra LD Auto bearing No. KA-03-AG-2560 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.

entities.text: Sharath Kumar R vs Ramakrishna on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Nagarbhavi Fortis Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and spent Rs.1,40,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as Service Advisor at Adishakthi Auto Zone Showroom and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent is the RC owner of the Ape auto bearing No. KA-03-AG-2560 is liable to pay compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.

3. After service of notice, respondent appeared through his counsel, but in spite of sufficient opportunity has not filed any written statement and also not chosen to cross-examine the Pw.1 or to lead the defence evidence.

4. The following points arises for consideration:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 26.7.2021 at about 2.20 p.m. when he was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing No. KA-41-EQ-1389 on Mysore road to Nayandahalli, at that time the driver of Ape auto bearing No. KA-03- AG-2560 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what rate and from whom?
3. What Order or award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 8.

Also examined Dr. Manjunath K.L. as PW.2 through him got marked Ex.P9 to 11.
6.
Heard the arguments.
7. My findings on the above points are as under.

Point No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Point No.2 : Partly in the affirmative,
Point No.3 : As per the final orders Sharath Kumar R vs Ramakrishna on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167837568/
2  for the following:-

: R E A S O N S:
 POINT NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced copies of complaint, FIR, wound certificate, order sheet in CC. No. 5349-2021, charge sheet, spot mahazar along with sketch and IMV report, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to P7 .
9.
As per the documents, on the basis of Ex.P1 complaint, police registered the FIR against the driver of the Ape auto bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AG-2560.
The contents of Ex.P1 complaint and Ex.P2 FIR supports the case of the petitioner about the alleged accident and negligence on the part of the driver of Ape auto bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AG-2560.
After the registration of FIR, the police conducted the spot mahazar and also drawn rough sketch as per Ex.P6.
On perusal of Ex.P6- spot mahazar and rough sketch the driver of Ape auto bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AG-2560 came from opposite direction and dashed against the bike of the petitioner.
As per the contents of Ex.P6 the driver of the ape auto bearing No. KA-03-AG-2560 came in a one way road.
Thus, it holds that the accident is caused by the negligence of the driver of Ape auto.

10. The contents of Ex.P6 spot mahazar and rough sketch & Ex.P7 IMV report supports the allegation of the petitioner about the negligence driving of the driver of the Ape auto bearing Reg.
No. KA-03-AG-2560.
No grounds are made out by the driver of the offending vehicle to disprove the said allegations.

After the detailed investigation the charge sheet is also came to be filed against the rider of the Ape auto bearing Reg. No. KA- 03-AG-2560 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279,
338 of IPC 185, 150 R/w Sec. 177 3 (1) , R/w. Sec. 181, 146, R/w. Sec. 196, 56, R/w. Sec. 192, 5 R/w.
Sec. 180 of MV Act.
11.

It is necessary to state, even at the cost of repetition that the Police who registered the FIR on the basis of first information has charge sheeted the driver of Ape auto bearing No. KA-03-AG-2560,
thereby prima facie opining that the said accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of driver of the Ape auto bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AG-2560.

In this case it is very important to note that the respondent who is the owner of the said offending Ape auto has neither examined himself or the driver of said Ape auto to show that the accident is caused by the negligence of the petitioner.
In the charge sheet the respondent is made as accused No.2 for not having the insurance to the offending Ape auto.

12. The respondent also an accused remained silent and has not denied by filing the written statement and thereby has not availed the chance of cross examining the P.W.1 and this goes to show that respondent do not dispute the facts asserted by the PW.1 and there is nothing on record on the basis of which it can be said that the negligence on the part of the petitioner led to the Sharath Kumar R vs Ramakrishna on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167837568/
3 accident.
13.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
12.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW1 and AW2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the chargesheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.

14. Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 7, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing No. KA-03-AG-2560.

15. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
17. As per well settled principle of law the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence there are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner.

All the materials available on record leading to show that,
petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 26.7.2021 which is caused by the Sharath Kumar R vs Ramakrishna on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167837568/
4 driver of the Ape auto bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AG- 2560 which belonging to respondent.

entities.text: Sharath Kumar R vs Ramakrishna on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
Immediately after the accident the petitioner admitted to Fortis Hospital for the treatment.
The contents of Ex.P3 -wound certificate and Ex.P.11 inpatient case sheet also tallies with Ex.P1 & 2- complaint and FIR about the alleged accident.
18. The respondent even after service of summons remained silent and has not made any grounds to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner.
Thus, it shows that the respondent herein has no grounds for defence and has not disputed the allegations of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative.

POINT NO.2:
19.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the vehicle of respondent.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
20. The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P3 which shows that the petitioner sustained communited fracture both bone left forearm.

Further the petitioner has also produced discharge summary as per Ex.P11- which shows that the petitioner was admitted to the hospital on 26.7.2021 and discharged on 28.7.2021.
21.
According to the petitioner he was working as Service advisor and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But to prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.

22. While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
(A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.3 and 11- wound certificate and discharge summary which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained grievous injury.

Hence keeping in mind the injury mentioned in wound certificate and discharge summary, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.10,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has not produced medical bills hence, he is not entitle for compensation under this head.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as Service advisor and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.

To consider the avocation of the Sharath Kumar R vs Ramakrishna on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167837568/
5 petitioner except the oral evidence, no documents or proof of salary is shown by the petitioner.
Such being the case it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2021.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P11- the petitioner was admitted to Fortis Hospital on 26.7.2021 and discharged on 28.7.2021 for 3 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence this court is of the opinion that in total one month may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.Manjunath K.L, Orthopedic Surgeon at Fortis Hospital, Nagarbhavi, Bengaluru, as PW.2,
through him assessment letter, X- ray film and inpatient case sheet are marked under Ex.P.9 to 11.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained pain and difficulty in moving left wrist and forearm, abnormal mobility and crepitus of left forearm, painful movements of wrist and punctured wound over forearm.
He underwent open reduction and fixation done with plate and screws and bone grafting.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability of left upper limb at 31% and whole body disability at 8%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
By considering the same this court is of the opinion that the disability would be 8% in this case by considering the age and avocation of the petitioner.
As per the Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P9, as per this document the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 13.09.1991.
The accident was occurred in the year-2021.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 31 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '16'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.15,000/- X 12 X 16 X 8% =Rs.2,30,400/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ; As per Ex.P11 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 3 days.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P3 the injury sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.
No other evidence is placed by the respondent to disbelieve the evidence of the doctor in this regard.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner was admitted as inpatient for 3 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the grievous injuries as discussed above, one month of healing period including the inpatient period may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.3,000/- in total.

Sharath Kumar R vs Ramakrishna on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167837568/
6
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.10,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses:
PW.2 in his affidavit evidence has stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.50,000/-.
Hence, by looking to the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment taken by him, I inclined to award Rs.20,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 10,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses NIL c) Towards loss of income Rs. 15,000/-
d) Towards disability Rs. 2,30,400/-
e) Towards food, nourishment  and conveyance Rs. 10,000/-
f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 3,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 10,000/-
h) Towards future medical  expenses Rs. 20,000/-
 _______________
. The respondent being the RC owner of the Ape auto bearing No. KA-03-AG-2560.

The charge sheet is against the respondent herein by invoking Sec. 5 R/w.
Sec. 180 & 146 R/w. 186 of IMV Act for allowing the person to drive the said ape auto without having valid insurance to the Ape auto at the time of accident.
Hence, being the RC owner the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this point answered partly in the affirmative.

Sharath Kumar R vs Ramakrishna on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167837568/

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following;
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,98,400/- (Rupees Two lakhs ninety eight thousand four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

b) Towards medical expenses NIL c) Towards loss of income Rs. 15,000/-
d) Towards disability Rs. 2,30,400/-
e) Towards food, nourishment  and conveyance Rs. 10,000/-
f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 3,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 10,000/-
h) Towards future medical  expenses Rs. 20,000/-
 _______________
Hence, being the RC owner the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this point answered partly in the affirmative.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following;
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,98,400/- (Rupees Two lakhs ninety eight thousand four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
